steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper proposing "Immunity", a Mixture-of-Experts based defense against adversarial attacks on deep neural networks. Motivate adversarial robustness, review the main categories of existing defenses and their limits, describe our approach, list our contributions, and give the paper outline.

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Deep neural networks (DNNs) have shown remarkable capabilities and they are used everywhere in many domains, such as medical diagnosis, autonomous driving, security surveillance, etc. But recent studies have shown that DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Adversarial attacks put imperceptible perturbations into the original input data and make DNNs produce wrong outputs or predictions. These attacks undermine the effectiveness and reliability of DNNs, and they also cause risks in safety-critical scenarios where these models are used, like medical misdiagnosis, traffic accidents, and information leakage. So enhancing the adversarial robustness of DNNs, which means making these models stronger against different adversarial attacks, is an important but challenging problem.

Many adversarial defense strategies have been proposed for this problem so far, and they can mainly be put into 3 approaches: robust optimization, data compression and auxiliary means. Robust optimization trains the model with adversarial examples or regularizers to make it more adaptable and generalizable. Data compression alleviates harmful data and reduces the perturbations. Auxiliary means add extra mechanisms to improve model complexity and reliability. But the existing methods have some limitations. For example, robust optimization has a risk of overfitting or of lowering accuracy, data compression can lose useful information or features, and auxiliary means can add computational overhead or only be applicable in limited cases. Also, existing methods don't fully consider how the model architecture and behavior affect robustness, or how different parts of the input data contribute to robustness.

- Immunity
  - name: Innovative MoE with MUtual info & positioN stabilITY
  - multiple sub-models (expert networks): disentangle features, extract unique concepts/semantics
  - key innovation: Random Switch Gate instead of deterministic gate, coordinates + aggregates experts

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Deep neural networks (DNNs) have shown remarkable capabilities and they are used everywhere in many domains, such as medical diagnosis, autonomous driving, security surveillance, etc. But recent studies have shown that DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Adversarial attacks put imperceptible perturbations into the original input data and make DNNs produce wrong outputs or predictions. These attacks undermine the effectiveness and reliability of DNNs, and they also cause risks in safety-critical scenarios where these models are used, like medical misdiagnosis, traffic accidents, and information leakage. So enhancing the adversarial robustness of DNNs, which means making these models stronger against different adversarial attacks, is an important but challenging problem.

Many adversarial defense strategies have been proposed for this problem so far, and they can mainly be put into 3 approaches: robust optimization, data compression and auxiliary means. Robust optimization trains the model with adversarial examples or regularizers to make it more adaptable and generalizable. Data compression alleviates harmful data and reduces the perturbations. Auxiliary means add extra mechanisms to improve model complexity and reliability. But the existing methods have some limitations. For example, robust optimization has a risk of overfitting or of lowering accuracy, data compression can lose useful information or features, and auxiliary means can add computational overhead or only be applicable in limited cases. Also, existing methods don't fully consider how the model architecture and behavior affect robustness, or how different parts of the input data contribute to robustness.

To deal with these limitations, we propose a new approach called "Immunity" (Innovative MoE with MUtual info & positioN stabilITY) that makes models better at defending against adversarial attacks. Immunity uses multiple sub-models, called expert networks, to disentangle distinct features and extract unique concepts or semantics, and this makes the model more robust. The key innovation in our Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture is that we use a Random Switch Gate instead of a deterministic gate to coordinate and aggregate the outputs of the individual experts. During inference it randomly exchanges weights to improve robustness. To enhance multi-angle learning further, we design a new Mutual Information (MI) loss and a position-stability loss based on Grad-CAM. These losses directly regularize the heatmap of the expert network, which increases the diversity and causality of the learned representations.

The main innovations and contributions of this paper are:

- We propose a new "Immunity" approach that adds Random Switch Gates into the MoE architecture to enhance both adversarial robustness and interpretability, which gives new insights on using the diversity of model ensembles for defense.

- We design a new MI-based loss that works on Grad-CAM. It makes the calculation simpler and has a smaller negative impact on predictions than the prevailing MI losses. We also formulate a position-stability regularizer that encourages the expert networks to learn causal representations.

- We do extensive experiments on public datasets and show that Immunity significantly outperforms state-of-the-art defense methods against different adversarial attacks, in both standard and adversarial training settings. Our approach is consistently better at defending against various attack types and magnitudes.

The rest of this paper is organized like this: Section 2 reviews related prior works. Section 3 gives background and motivations. Section 4 explains the principles and details of the proposed method "Immunity". Section 5 presents the experimental setup and results in detail. Finally, Section 6 concludes the paper.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Deep neural networks (DNNs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities and ubiquitous applications across various domains, including medical diagnosis [1], autonomous driving [2], security surveillance [3], etc. However, recent studies have revealed that DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks [4]. Adversarial attacks craft imperceptible perturbations into the original input data and induce DNNs to generate erroneous outputs or predictions [5]. These attacks not only undermine the effectiveness and reliability of DNNs, but also pose risks in safety-critical scenarios involving these models, such as medical misdiagnosis, traffic accidents, and information leakage [6]. Therefore, enhancing the adversarial robustness of DNNs, i.e. strengthening these models against diverse adversarial attacks, is an important yet challenging problem.

To date, many adversarial defense strategies have emerged to address this problem, and they can be principally classified into 3 main approaches: robust optimization, data compression and auxiliary means [7]. Robust optimization trains the model using adversarial examples or regularizers to enhance adaptability and generalizability [8] [9]. Data compression alleviates harmful data and reduces perturbations [10]. Auxiliary means incorporate additional mechanisms to improve model complexity and reliability [11]. However, existing methods have certain limitations. For instance, robust optimization risks overfitting or compromising accuracy [12], data compression may lose useful information or features [13], and auxiliary means can impose computational overhead or have limited applicability [14]. Moreover, existing methods do not fully consider how model architecture and behavior influence robustness, or how different components of the input data contribute to robustness.

To address these limitations, we propose a novel approach termed "Immunity" (Innovative MoE with MUtual info & positioN stabilITY) that enhances model defense against adversarial attacks. Immunity enhances model robustness by employing multiple sub-models, termed expert networks, to disentangle distinct features and extract unique concepts or semantics. The key innovation in our Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture is integrating a Random Switch Gate, instead of a deterministic gate, to coordinate and aggregate the outputs of individual experts. During inference, it randomly exchanges weights to improve robustness. To further enhance multi-angle learning, we devise a novel Mutual Information (MI) loss and a position-stability loss based on Grad-CAM. These losses directly regularize the heatmap of the expert network to increase the diversity and causality of learned representations.

The core innovations and contributions of this paper are:

- We propose a novel "Immunity" approach that incorporates Random Switch Gates into the MoE architecture to jointly enhance adversarial robustness and interpretability, providing new insights into leveraging model ensemble diversity for defense.

- We devise a novel MI-based loss operating on Grad-CAM, which simplifies calculation and has a subtler negative impact on predictions than prevailing MI losses. We also formulate a position-stability regularizer that encourages expert networks to learn causal representations.

- Through extensive experiments on public datasets, we demonstrate that Immunity significantly outperforms state-of-the-art defense methods against diverse adversarial attacks under both standard and adversarial training settings. Our approach is consistently superior in defending against various attack types and magnitudes.

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows: Section 2 reviews related prior work. Section 3 provides background and motivations. Section 4 elaborates on the principles and details of the proposed method "Immunity". Section 5 presents the experimental setup and results in detail. Finally, Section 6 concludes the paper.
